intended_object: For a group scheme G over a field K, the subgroup G°(K) ⊆ G(K) of K-rational points of the identity component G°, i.e. the image of G°(K) → G(K). Inferred from the docstring and from its use in `rationalComponentGroup` (G(K)/G°(K)) in the module on component groups (Milne §2g).
explanation:
I read the body and the definitions it relies on. `groupSchemePoints f` is the hom-set `𝟙_ ⟶ Over.mk f` in `Over (Spec K)`, i.e. the group G(K) of K-rational points. `Scheme.identityComponentι` is the open (and closed) immersion of the identity component G° into G, made into a subgroup object. `IsMonHom.monoidHom ι (𝟙_)` is the group homomorphism G°(K) → G(K) given by composing with ι. Its `.range` is therefore the set of K-points of G that factor through G°, which is exactly G°(K) as a subgroup of G(K). The private lemma `exists_identityComponentPoint_iff` confirms this: a point is in the range exactly when its underlying point lies in G°.

There are two extra typeclass assumptions. `LocallyConnectedSpace G` is what makes the connected component of the identity an open subscheme, so the identity component can be defined at all. Connectedness of G° ×_K G° is needed to put a group structure on G°. For group schemes over a field this second condition always holds, because G° is geometrically connected. So both are technical hypotheses of the library's API. They do not change the object on the inputs where it is defined.

On generality: the notion of K-rational points of the identity component is naturally stated over a base field, and the whole module is about the rational component group G(K)/G°(K). So working over `Spec K` is the natural setting, not a restriction. Mathlib has no counterpart for identity components of group schemes.
